caption: Atharvaveda 1.6.1, the water mantra
intro: This is a mantra from the **Atharvaveda** (Atharvaveda 1.6.1, the water mantra). Below are the Sanskrit text and a **plain English meaning**.
takeaways: The four Vedas are Rigveda, Yajurveda, Samaveda and Atharvaveda.
Vedic mantras are learned by listening and repeating.

p: **ॐ शं नो देवीरभिष्टय आपो भवन्तु पीतये । शं योरभि स्रवन्तु नः ॥**
May the divine waters be good for us, for our wishes and for drinking. May they flow to us with health and joy.
The Atharvaveda is one of the four Vedas, the oldest scriptures of Sanatana Dharma, handed down by voice for thousands of years.

faq.a: May the divine waters be good for us, for our wishes and for drinking. May they flow to us with health and joy.
There are **four**: Rig, Yajur, Sama and Atharva.

note: The Sanskrit is the traditional text. The English is our own plain rendering.
